findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises ValueError (500)
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start: `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing; this raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The endpoint's `paginate()` helper only converts `BadPaginationError` into a 400, so any client that supplies a cursor with a negative offset (cursors are user-supplied strings and `Cursor.from_string` happily parses `-5`) gets an unhandled 500. The inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong and should not be used to justify this branch.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is numeric-only but is used with a datetime order_by
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, self.key))` and `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (the integer/float `Paginator` semantics). The only caller, `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`, uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`. Consequences: (1) `math.ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError` for any non-empty result page, so the first optimized request 500s; (2) even if that were fixed, `value_from_cursor` would feed a raw number into the raw SQL comparison built by `build_queryset` (`"datetime" <= %s`), which fails/compares wrongly against a timestamp column. For a datetime sort key the class must derive from `DateTimePaginator` (or override these two methods with the timestamp-multiplier logic).

findings.title: Privilege gate uses request.user.is_superuser and member.has_global_access
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is described as gating "authorized administrators", but neither condition expresses that. Sentry requires superuser mode to be actively elevated for a request; the correct check is `is_active_superuser(request)` (or an explicit scope check). Reading `request.user.is_superuser` grants the privileged code path to any staff account with a normal, non-elevated session. Additionally, `has_global_access` on an org member only means "access to all teams" and is implicitly true for every member of an organization with open membership, so the second clause makes the gate effectively 'any member', not 'admin'. If the advanced pagination path is meant to be restricted, gate it on an explicit permission/scope instead.

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None -> AttributeError 500
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional and is `None` for requests that are not made by an org member (e.g. token/integration or org-auth-token authenticated requests, or a user acting through superuser without membership). In that case this line raises `AttributeError` and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the audit log. The attribute access also needs verification that `has_global_access` exists on the RPC member model at all, since it is a property of the Django `OrganizationMember` model rather than a field of the RPC payload.

findings.title: Cursor values become incompatible depending on an undeclared query parameter
findings.body: The new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter switches between `DateTimePaginator` (cursor values are millisecond timestamps) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (cursor values are raw numeric keys). Cursors returned by one paginator are therefore meaningless to the other, so a client that follows a `Link` header but drops/keeps the flag inconsistently (or a cached/bookmarked cursor) will silently page to the wrong position rather than erroring. The parameter is also not declared in `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`, so it is undocumented and unvalidated (any value other than the exact string "true" silently falls back). Either encode the mode in the cursor/Link headers or drop the request-level switch.

findings.title: Inconsistent and silent clamping of negative offsets in BasePaginator
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes behaviour for every paginator derived from `BasePaginator`. For forward cursors an invalid negative offset is now silently clamped to 0, so a malformed/tampered cursor returns page 1 instead of surfacing an error - and the `next`/`prev` cursors are then built from `cursor.offset` (still negative) in `build_cursor`, producing further inconsistent cursors. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed straight into `queryset[offset:stop]`, which raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` and yields a 500. Negative offsets should be rejected explicitly (e.g. `raise BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`, as `OffsetPaginator` and `ChainPaginator` already do) rather than half-clamped; the comment claiming "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions" is incorrect.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (including the negative-offset branch and the `enable_advanced_features` flag) and the new conditional path in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` are added with no accompanying tests. Nothing exercises the optimized path, which is why the datetime/`math.ceil` TypeError and the negative-slice ValueError went unnoticed; there is also no test asserting that unprivileged callers cannot activate the path. Tests covering: optimized path with results, cursor round-tripping, negative offsets, and the authorization gate are needed before merging.

findings.title: Comment claims a behaviour change that the code does not make
findings.body: The added comment in `Cursor.__init__` states "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but the code is unchanged (`self.offset = int(offset)`) - no validation was removed or added, and nothing in `Cursor` makes negative offsets usable (consumers slice QuerySets, which reject negative starts). A comment that describes a non-existent feature will mislead future readers into assuming negative offsets are a supported, safe input. Remove it or replace it with an accurate note (ideally a validation that rejects negative offsets).
